headline: Maersk Breached by Ransomware, Microsoft Issues Record Patch for Outlook Zero-Day
summary: In the last 48 hours, the cybersecurity landscape has been dominated by significant breaches and critical vulnerabilities. Shipping giant Maersk confirmed a data breach by the WhiteArmor ransomware group, who are demanding a $5 million ransom. Microsoft released its largest-ever Patch Tuesday, fixing 1,235 flaws, including an actively exploited Outlook zero-day. Concurrently, a massive supply chain attack on GitHub is compromising thousands of repositories, and numerous Philippine government agencies are investigating extensive data breaches. These events highlight persistent threats from ransomware, supply chain attacks, and unpatched zero-day vulnerabilities.

articles.headline: 'Black October' Attacks Steal API Keys from Nine AI Dev Platforms
articles.title: Black October: Coordinated Attacks on AI Developer Platforms
articles.excerpt: A coordinated wave of attacks dubbed "Black October" has compromised at least nine AI developer platforms, including Northflank, Railway, and Lightning AI. Security researchers at Wiz, who identified the campaign, report that attackers targeted environment variables to steal API keys and other secrets. This technique, termed "LLMJacking," allows threat actors to hijack expensive AI model services for their own use, leading to significant fraudulent charges for victims. Northflank confirmed the breach after being alerted by Wiz, noting that multiple customers had reported unauthorized use of their AI API keys. The campaign highlights a critical credential crisis in AI infrastructure, with some attacks employing "agent swarm" tactics and resulting in at least one platform, Zeabur, shutting down permanently.
articles.updateSummary: Railway platform breach details reveal $740k in fraudulent AI charges and GitHub token exposure, significantly increasing the campaign's known financial impact.
articles.updateContent: New details have emerged regarding the breach of the Railway cloud hosting platform, a victim of the 'Black October' campaign. Attackers exploited a chain of two vulnerabilities to access customer environment variables, specifically targeting AI service API keys. This resulted in approximately $740,000 in fraudulent AI service charges, a substantial increase from the previously reported overall campaign impact. Additionally, the breach exposed GitHub OAuth tokens for 1,852 users. Railway has remediated the vulnerabilities and committed to covering the fraudulent costs, highlighting the severe financial liabilities associated with compromised AI API keys.

articles.headline: Email Service Breach Leaks 77 Million Addresses, Sparks Phishing Wave
articles.title: Arara Message Breach Exposes 77 Million Email Addresses
articles.excerpt: Paycloud Holdings, parent company of the Arara Message email distribution service in Japan, has disclosed a data breach exposing approximately 77 million email addresses. Information from 380 corporate clients was also compromised, though no credit card data was lost. Following the breach, attackers launched a large-scale phishing campaign, sending over 7 million emails impersonating a credit card company to the leaked addresses. Users are warned to be vigilant against suspicious communications.
articles.updateSummary: SEGA confirms 2.2 million customer emails exposed via the previously reported Arara Message data breach, increasing phishing risk.
articles.updateContent: Video game company SEGA announced on November 9, 2026, that 2,196,044 customer email addresses were compromised due to the data breach at its third-party newsletter provider, Arara Co., Ltd. This confirms SEGA as one of the 380 corporate clients affected by the larger Arara incident that exposed 77 million emails. Attackers leveraged Arara's compromised infrastructure to send highly convincing phishing emails, posing a significant risk to SEGA's affected customers. The incident highlights the ongoing impact of the Arara breach on its clients.

articles.headline: Ten Philippine Government Agencies Report Data Breaches
articles.title: Philippines Confirms Data Breaches Across 10 Government Agencies
articles.excerpt: The Philippines' National Privacy Commission (NPC) has confirmed that ten government agencies, including the Department of Justice and the Department of Information and Communications Technology, have filed data breach notifications. The NPC is now assessing the scope and nature of the incidents, which raise serious concerns about the security of sensitive government-held data. The full extent of the breaches and the number of affected individuals have not yet been disclosed.
articles.updateSummary: NPC confirms data breaches now include several state universities, exposing extensive PII, student, and employee records.
articles.updateContent: The National Privacy Commission (NPC) has confirmed that the ongoing data breach investigation now includes several state universities, in addition to the ten government agencies previously reported. This expansion significantly increases the scope of the incident. The compromised data is reported to be extensive, including personally identifiable information (PII), government ID numbers, taxpayer information, HR and payroll records, and student files. The breaches were initially flagged by the cybersecurity monitoring group Deep Web Konek. New technical analysis points to potential exploitation of public-facing applications or large-scale phishing campaigns.

articles.headline: Microsoft Patches Actively Exploited Outlook Zero-Day in Massive Update
articles.title: Microsoft Patches Outlook Zero-Day CVE-2026-124194 for NTLM Hash Theft
articles.excerpt: Microsoft's November 2026 Patch Tuesday addressed over 1,200 vulnerabilities, including a critical zero-day in Outlook, CVE-2026-124194, which is being actively exploited. The flaw allows attackers to steal NTLM authentication hashes by tricking users into opening a malicious message file. The vulnerability does not trigger in the Preview Pane, requiring direct user interaction. In response, CISA has added CVE-2026-124194 to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities (KEV) catalog, mandating federal agencies to patch by November 24, 2026.
articles.updateSummary: New critical RCE vulnerability (CVE-2026-116928) in Windows Search Component disclosed, affecting Exchange servers.
articles.updateContent: The November 2026 Patch Tuesday update now includes details on a critical Remote Code Execution (RCE) vulnerability, CVE-2026-116928, in the Windows Search Component. This flaw, rated CVSS 9.8, allows an attacker to achieve code execution on on-premise Microsoft Exchange Servers without any user interaction by sending a specially crafted email. This significantly broadens the impact and severity of the patch cycle beyond the previously reported Outlook zero-day. The update also confirms a total of 1,235 CVEs were patched, including 66 critical vulnerabilities.

articles.headline: Vanderbilt University Hit by BYOD Ransomware; Attackers Claim Massive Data Theft
articles.title: BYOD Ransomware Gang Claims Attack on Vanderbilt University
articles.excerpt: Vanderbilt University is recovering from a major ransomware attack claimed by the 'BYOD' group, which began on November 9, 2026. The incident caused widespread system disruptions, forcing the university to shut down devices and network access. The BYOD gang alleges it exfiltrated a massive trove of data, including over one million Social Security numbers, student records, and research data. While Vanderbilt has begun restoring services, it has not confirmed the data theft claims. The attack follows a pattern of the BYOD group targeting higher education and healthcare.
articles.updateSummary: Vanderbilt confirms incident on Nov 11; new hunting hints for AD recon tools provided.
articles.updateContent: New reports clarify Vanderbilt University confirmed the ransomware incident on November 11, 2026, with the attack also stated to have begun on this date, differing from earlier reports of November 9. Additional cyber observables for hunting include `adfind.exe` and `bloodhound.exe` for Active Directory reconnaissance, `*.byod` file extensions, and monitoring for internal RDP connections. The university continues to work on containment and investigation, with D3FEND techniques like Resource Access Pattern Analysis and Data Backup highlighted for detection and mitigation.

articles.headline: Maersk Confirms Breach; WhiteArmor Ransomware Demands $5M Ransom
articles.title: Maersk Breach: WhiteArmor Ransomware Claims 100GB Data Theft
articles.excerpt: Global shipping firm Maersk has confirmed a data breach affecting a legacy IT system from a previous acquisition. The WhiteArmor ransomware group claims to have stolen 100GB of sensitive logistics data, including plaintext passwords and customer records, and is demanding a $5 million ransom. Maersk states the incident is isolated and does not anticipate disruption to customer operations, though the attackers have published detailed lists of allegedly stolen data to apply pressure.

articles.headline: Massive GitHub Supply Chain Attack Injects 'wfx' Stealer into Repos
articles.title: GitHub Supply Chain Attack Steals CI/CD Secrets with 'wfx' Malware
articles.excerpt: A large-scale software supply chain attack is actively targeting the GitHub ecosystem. Attackers are using compromised developer accounts to inject a sophisticated information stealer, dubbed 'wfx', into tens of thousands of code repositories. The malware is designed to run within GitHub Actions to exfiltrate sensitive CI/CD secrets, including repository secrets, cloud credentials, and API keys, posing a severe threat to software development and deployment pipelines.

articles.headline: Microsoft Reveals 'Lazarus,' a Stealthy AI Supply Chain Attack
articles.title: Microsoft's 'Lazarus' Attack Can Backdoor AI Models by Editing Neurons
articles.excerpt: Microsoft researchers have disclosed 'Lazarus,' a novel and highly stealthy AI supply-chain attack technique. The method allows an attacker to surgically backdoor open-weight large language models (LLMs) by modifying fewer than ten dormant neurons. This nearly undetectable edit, which requires no model retraining, can be activated by a secret trigger in a prompt, forcing the AI agent to execute arbitrary commands using its assigned privileges. The research highlights a critical new threat vector for the rapidly growing field of agentic AI.

articles.headline: Falcon C2 Framework Compromises Browsers to Target Governments
articles.title: Falcon C2: Browser-Based Framework Targets Governments
articles.excerpt: Unit 42 has identified a browser-based command and control (C2) framework named Falcon (also known as XG or Xiàng Gē). The threat actor leverages this framework to compromise government webmail portals and applications by injecting malicious JavaScript. Operating entirely within the browser, Falcon can sideload malicious Chrome extensions and exfiltrate sensitive information. The campaign, observed between March and May 2026, targeted government ministries in the Middle East and Southeast Asia. The framework also serves as a delivery mechanism for a secondary implant called Antino, which uses Microsoft OneDrive for C2 communications. Analysis reveals a high-confidence link between Falcon and the PeckBirdy framework previously reported by Trend Micro.
